description: Hello everyone, I am a developer holding a B.S. in Software Development who primarily focuses on Java and Python. I am looking for individuals passionate about software and design in the healthcare sphere or who would like to try creating something within different parameters. All experience levels are welcome, just bring ideas and an attitude to try and learn.
summary: Long missions to the Moon and Mars expose astronauts to radiation, isolation, altered gravity and much more, which affect their health. Astra Health is a web app that lets astronauts log daily health readings, monitor their status on a color-coded dashboard and a clickable body figure. Additionally, guidance is provided on why each reading matters in space and when to contact the appropriate party. Thresholds are based on NASA and ESA research and adjusted for how spaceflight changes the body.
details:
Astra Health is a health self-check web app for astronauts on long-duration missions. Which contains the following pages:

  • Landing page: which allows astronauts to declare who they are and acces the health form
  • Health Form: Provides sections to input data on health questions. The data they enter is then referenced against stored data within the JSON that holds parameters for certain health checks and conditions.
  • Health Dashboard: Displays health information for the astronaut to see. Allows an individual to determine if they are in critical condition or approaching it. There is also a body figure which is clickable. It gives a more detailed synopsis on the importance of the body locations' health check, and depending on the health status, it may suggest next steps for treatment.

The Web Application:
Just plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript (ES modules), with no backend. All indicator data (units, status thresholds, explanations and guidance) lives in one JSON file (the JSON was generated from NASA and Space agency data, and constructed by Anthropic Claude Chat. The form, cards, and body figure are based on the data from the JSON file. New indicators can be added without changing code. Readings are saved locally in the browser.

What makes it space-specific

  • Core body temperature rises about 1 °C in space, so temperature thresholds are shifted up to avoid false fever alerts.
  • Insulin resistance develops in flight, so fasting glucose is tracked.
  • Fluid shifts toward the head lower 24-hour blood pressure and change how the heart works.
  • NASA schedules 8.5 hours of sleep, but astronauts average about 6.
  • Isolation, confinement and distance from Earth strain mood and behavioral health.
    Each indicator is linked to NASA’s Human Research Program hazards.

Benefits
On deep-space missions, communication delays mean astronauts can’t always wait for Earth. Astra Health gives simple instructions on how to measure each indicator, explains results, and indicates when someone may need further attention.

What we hope to achieve
We hope Astra Health shows how simple, research-based self-checks could help crews catch health problems early when help from Earth is minutes away. The app is also extremely expandable, so features such as log-keeping, journaling, and radiation detection can be implemented using NASA’s DONKI space weather data.

Tools
HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Visual Studio Code with Live Server, GitHub, a domain from the GoDaddy Registry Global Offer hosted on Porkbun, and Google Fonts (Intel One Mono). All artwork is original and hand-drawn by Ashly. Code is provided by Violet, with small snippets taken from Claude Code, along with use for debugging and strucutre.
